claims.summary: The origin limits liability to the sponsor of an electioneering communication, making a medium liable only if it strips disclosures or alters content into synthetic media; the descendant lacks this.
The descendant defines school employee (excluding students), depicted individual, digital depiction, and information content providers; the origin has none of these terms.
The descendant begins defining an intimate digital depiction as a digital depiction created or altered by digital means; the origin has no such definition.
The origin carries a separately lettered definition of information content provider after the interactive computer service definition; the descendant has no matching definition at that point.
The origin assigns liability for electioneering communications to the sponsor rather than the disseminating medium, with exceptions; the descendant has no such liability provision.
The descendant defines a school-employee term (excluding enrolled students), "depicted individual," "digital depiction," and "intimate digital depiction"; the origin has none of these.
Both define "information content provider" in the same substance; the origin places it after the interactive computer service definition, the descendant before it, in plural form.
The origin gives the interactive computer service definition as lettered item (b) using "means"; the descendant numbers it (4) without "means."
